title: Previous-year runoff reduced annual reconstruction error against two weather models in 309 Australian catchments in 2001-2021
abstract: We tested whether previous-year runoff adds information beyond observed weather in annual runoff estimates. We used CAMELS-AUS v2.03 daily data. Each test year in 2001-2021 used only earlier targets from 1971 onward for fitting. The test retained 6030 site-years in 309 catchments. The longer weather model used current rainfall, squared rainfall, reference evapotranspiration, three earlier rainfall totals, and the cool-season rainfall share. Adding previous-year square-root runoff reduced mean squared error by 11.54%. The conditional 95% three-year block interval was 8.09% to 14.92%. Errors were measured in square-root runoff units and scaled by each site's earlier variation. Only 52.43% of sites improved; the median site gain was 0.55%. This is a reconstruction with observed target-year weather. It does not establish a lead forecast, groundwater cause, or drought recovery. A short test period, selected catchments, source errors, calendar-year boundaries, and model choice limit inference. The package gives code, aggregate errors, uncertainty draws, exact source hashes, and a retrieval script.

display.caption: Error reduction when previous-year runoff is added. Bars show conditional 95% three-year block intervals. Target-year weather is observed.
